reuse.why: Ignores the existing exported getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts (which already handles missing, numeric and ranged amounts and is used by the UI) and adds a near-identical getScheduleAmount beside it.

duplication.why: Collapses four inline copies into one new helper, but that helper duplicates getScheduledAmount, leaving two parallel amount resolvers with different range rules.

placement.why: The new helper is placed in shared/schedules.ts, the right module for schedule amount logic.

scope.why: Only the amount resolution sites, the helper and its tests are touched.

maintainability.why: Two similarly named helpers (getScheduleAmount vs getScheduledAmount) now encode different rules, and the UI and the budget schedule template still use the midpoint, a confusing split for maintainers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts adds getScheduleAmount instead of changing getScheduledAmount; server/budget/schedule-template.ts and desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount still compute the midpoint.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduleAmount in shared/schedules.ts is a renamed copy of getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch with only the range branch changed.

one_place.where: The new rule lives in getScheduleAmount, but getScheduledAmount (SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile schedules, useScheduleEdit) and the inline midpoint in server/budget/schedule-template.ts still apply the old rule.
